answer: Rate-limit growth by terrain. Picture agent reputation as a hillside garden cut into terraces: an account may only add one new verified relationship per epoch, and the network's gale - a rotating beacon that re-samples which neighbors vouch - tears out any terrace whose links all appeared in the same burst. A farmer can sprint a thousand empty accounts up the slope, but weight only accrues terrace by terrace, one season at a time; to reach voting depth on N clones costs N sequential epochs of upkeep, no shortcut through bulk registration.
